h1: How to Organize Business Records Before Tax Filing
directAnswer: To organize business records before annual tax filing in Nepal, consolidate all serialized sales and purchase VAT registers, download and cross-match e-TDS withholding slips directly from the IRD portal, collect official bank balance confirmation letters, complete physical inventory valuation schedules, and prepare trial balance reconciliations for your statutory auditor.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.contentHtml:
Filing annual corporate returns (D-03) under the Income Tax Act 2058 requires methodical preparation before the statutory Poush 31 deadline:

Step 1: Complete Bank Reconciliation to Ashad 31

Every rupee transacted through company bank accounts must be accounted for and supported by matching vouchers and third-party bills.

Step 2: Cross-Check e-TDS on the IRD Portal

Log into the IRD Integrated Tax System (ITS). Verify that clients who deducted withholding tax on your bills have digitally verified the deposits under your PAN.

Step 3: Calculate Advance Tax Installments

Confirm that mandatory advance tax payments made in Poush (40%), Chaitra (70%), and Ashad (100%) are backed by valid bank deposit vouchers.

Step 4: Audit Schedule Preparation

Compile detailed schedules for fixed assets (with statutory depreciation under Schedule 2), aged trade debtors, trade creditors, and closing stock valuation.

Step 5: Obtain Tax Clearance Certificate (Kardata Pramanpatra)

Following audit completion and electronic D-03 filing, pay any residual income tax and generate the official digital Tax Clearance Certificate.

If audit compilation cannot be finalized by Poush 31, a formal extension of up to 3 months (until Chaitra end) can be requested under Section 98 of the Income Tax Act 2058. Discover our professional tax documentation review services.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for filing annual income tax returns late in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Under Section 117 of the Income Tax Act 2058, late filing incurs a penalty of NPR 100 per month or 0.1% of gross turnover per annum (whichever is higher), plus statutory interest on unpaid tax.
